title: Memory oscillation stabilizer: prefetch cohort throttles + staged fallback probe
creator: Sofia Reyes
description:
Problem: Intermittent OOMs in high-throughput serving caused by short-term memory oscillations when KV-prefetch and batching compete for GPU working set. Existing hard-eviction and global headroom heuristics either over-react (degrade quality) or under-react (OOMs).

Goal: Implement a memory-oscillation stabilizer that reduces OOM frequency without materially increasing latency or token cost by combining: (1) cohort-based prefetch budgets, (2) dampened admission smoothing (gamma scheduler), and (3) staged fallback probe with micro-model hedging and controlled retries. The approach favors graceful degradation and measurable rollback paths over aggressive global eviction.

Acceptance criteria: 
- 95% reduction in OOM incidents on canary workloads compared to baseline incident rate over 72h stress tests.
- P99 latency regression <= 10% on steady-state traffic.
- Token cost increase <= 5% for affected cohorts when stabilized.
- No customer-visible failed requests where a soft-degraded alternative exists (micro-model or partial output).

Design summary: 
1) Cohort prefetch budgets: classify requests into lightweight cohorts by request fingerprint (prompt length histogram + model variant + customer tier). Each cohort has a smoothing window and a dynamic prefetch allowance computed from moving-average memory pressure and recent KV hit-rate. Prefetch budgets are scaled down proactively for cohorts that exhibit oscillation patterns.

2) Gamma admission scheduler: replace instantaneous admission thresholds with a dampening integrator (gamma) that applies fractional adjustments to batch admission and KV materialization rates. This avoids step responses that lead to oscillation. Tunable parameters: gamma_alpha (0.1-0.4), lookback_seconds (5-30).

3) Staged fallback probe: when memory pressure crosses warning thresholds, run a short probe sequence per affected cohort: 
  - Stage A (fast): trim non-essential prompt prefixes (configurable trimming policy) and re-evaluate request.
  - Stage B (soft degrade): reduce batch window of the request (drop into smaller continuous-batch lane).
  - Stage C (micro-model hedging): route to quantized 4-bit micro-model variant that preserves core semantics for long-context hits.
  - Stage D (deferred retry): if all above fail, queue retry with exponential backoff + jitter to avoid thundering herd.
Probes record telemetry for each stage and select the least-degrading successful stage as the response path.

4) Safety: circuit-breaker with cooldown per cohort and global emergency lane that serves read-only cached prefixes (partial outputs) to provide graceful failure mode. All fallbacks are auditable and annotated in tracing for post-incident analysis.

Implementation plan: 
- Week 1: Build cohort classifier, gamma scheduler prototype in canary runtime, add telemetry hooks.
- Week 2: Implement staged fallback probe and micro-model routing, integrate with rollout flags.
- Week 3: Run adversarial stress tests (long-context adversarial prompts, large-batch spikes) and tune gamma parameters.
- Week 4: 5% canary A/B for 72h, collect metrics, iterate.

Testing and metrics: 
- Runbook for stress tests and incident playbook (link in comments).
- Dashboards: OOMs/million requests, cohort-level KV hit/miss, stage success rates, P99 latency and token cost delta.
- Fuzz tests: random long prompts and synthetic KV churn scenarios.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered: 
- Global aggressive eviction reduces OOMs but causes large quality regression; rejected for production baseline.
- Per-request strict reservation prevents OOMs but significantly reduces throughput; kept as emergency option.

Rollout: gated feature flagging per customer tier. Start with internal workloads, then a 5% canary on low-risk customers, then broad rollout if metrics meet acceptance criteria.

Artifacts: design doc (Confluence), perf dashboard, runbook, GitHub PR for the canary patch. See comments for links.
comments: 2026-02-10 Sofia Reyes: Created ticket after postmortem of incident #INC-2026-01 where two dedicated clusters hit OOM during a sudden KV churn event. Initial note: oscillation pattern looks like alternating aggressive prefetch + large microbatch windows. Assigned to Alex for prototype.

2026-02-12 Alex Chen: Spike implemented cohort classifier and simple moving-average prefetch throttle in canary runtime. Early tests show 30% reduction in OOM occurrence under synthetic noise but higher P99 on some cohorts. Pushed telemetry to perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/oom-stabilizer/canary-53799
2026-02-16 Priya Nair (SRE): Added emergency runbook entries for staged fallback probe. Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/ENG-53799+Runbook

2026-02-20 Alex Chen: Implemented gamma scheduler with configurable alpha and lookback. Benchmarked with adversarial long contexts (16k tokens) — gamma_alpha=0.25 reduced admission oscillation and stabilized memory usage during bursty traffic. Test results committed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8211

2026-02-25 Design feedback (Eleanor Park): Suggested making prefix trimming policy opt-in per model family to avoid breaking structured prompts. Decided to require model opt-in for Stage A trimming; updated design doc.

2026-03-02 Alex Chen: Added micro-model routing and hedging prototype (quantized-4bit tiny variant). Micro-model preserves summary-first fidelity in experiments. Observed token cost delta +2.1% when routing to micro-model vs baseline.
2026-03-05 Sofia Reyes (PM): Approved 5% canary plan for low-risk customers. Added monitoring thresholds and rollback criteria to release checklist.

2026-03-10 Alex Chen: Started 5% canary. First 48h: OOMs down 92% for canary cohorts, cohort-level P99 latency +6% on average. Two minor regressions traced to trimming stage over-aggressive rules; rolled back Stage A for model family 'code-transformer-v2'.

2026-03-12 Alex Chen: Iterated trimming policy to respect inline directives (<NO-TRIM> token) and re-enabled Stage A for most cohorts. Preparing PR for runtime-1.28 backport. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8287

2026-03-12 Priya Nair (SRE): Noted an incident learning: when micro-model is saturated in region, hedging to secondary region saved ~40% requests from failing. Plan to formalize cross-region hedging as a separate ticket.
